record.paper_title: Open Questions in Cosmic-Ray Research at Ultrahigh Energies
record.original_question: What are the strength, structure, and local-universe distribution of Galactic and extragalactic magnetic fields, and how do these fields deflect and time-delay ultrahigh-energy cosmic rays strongly enough to affect spectrum, composition, anisotropy, and the feasibility of charged-particle astronomy?

evidence.quote: Magnetic ﬁelds in scales comparable to and larger than the size of the Galaxy may affect the propagation of UHECRs.
Little is known about extragalactic magnetic ﬁelds (EGMFs).
Ultimately the deﬂection of UHECRs in EGMFs depends on the distribution of EGMFs in the local Universe.

Given the considerable uncertainties in the GMF and the inconclusive results on the effects of EGMFs on cosmic-ray propagation due to the model dependencies, the unambiguous identiﬁcation of individual UHECRs will require better constraints on EGMFs and improved models of the GMF.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Determine the strength, spatial structure, and local-universe distribution of Galactic and extragalactic magnetic fields, and quantify their effect on the propagation of ultrahigh-energy cosmic rays (charged nuclei with energies above roughly 10^18 eV). Specifically:

1. Provide a model of the Galactic magnetic field (GMF) consisting of a regular (coherent) component B_reg(x) and a turbulent component B_turb(x) defined on the Milky Way volume, including disk and halo contributions, with field strengths typically of order microgauss.

2. Provide a model of the extragalactic magnetic field (EGMF) B_ext(x) on the cosmological volume out to ~100 Mpc, characterized by a coherence length λ_B and an rms strength B_rms, including its correlation with the large-scale structure of the local universe (filaments, voids, clusters).

3. For a charged particle of charge Ze, energy E, and rigidity R = E/Z propagating along a path from a source at distance D to Earth, compute:
   (a) the integrated deflection angle θ(E,Z,direction) induced by B_reg and the rms deflection induced by B_turb and B_ext,
   (b) the time delay Δt(E,Z,D) relative to rectilinear propagation at the speed of light,
   (c) the resulting smearing of arrival directions and its impact on the observed energy spectrum, mass composition, and large- and small-scale anisotropies.

4. Determine quantitatively under what combinations of (B_reg, B_turb, B_ext, λ_B, source distribution, composition) the deflections are small enough (e.g., ≲ a few degrees at the highest rigidities) for charged-particle astronomy — i.e., the unambiguous identification of individual ultrahigh-energy cosmic-ray sources — to be feasible.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent reviews and modeling efforts (e.g., updated GMF models by Jansson–Farrar variants and 2024–2025 work on coherent+random Galactic fields, as well as constrained MHD simulations of the local extragalactic magnetic field) report that significant uncertainties remain in both Galactic and extragalactic magnetic field strength and structure, and that UHECR deflections—and thus the feasibility of charged-particle astronomy—are still model-dependent. The problem is widely regarded as open.

status_evidence.title: Ultra-high-energy cosmic rays (review)
status_evidence.snippet: Galactic and extragalactic magnetic fields remain poorly constrained, limiting source identification via UHECR arrival directions.
status_evidence.claim: Magnetic field uncertainties continue to dominate UHECR source-identification efforts.

status_evidence.title: Constrained simulations of the extragalactic magnetic field
status_evidence.snippet: Constrained MHD simulations of the local universe still yield order-of-magnitude uncertainties in EGMF strengths along UHECR sightlines.
status_evidence.claim: EGMF distribution in the local universe is not yet pinned down.
